fable.w: This section makes purely technical amendments to a Medicare payment formula in the Social Security Act, changing years, punctuation and percentage-point reductions. There is no tempting reading here: it mentions no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body or right to sue. No party outside the federal government is involved in any federal decision.
fable.s: Section 1886(r)(2)(B) of the Social Security Act, as added by section 3133, is amended

qwen_block.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to statutory text, specifically changing numerical values and punctuation in a formula for calculating payments. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory committees, or coordination with outside parties. The changes are purely legislative adjustments to existing rules.
qwen_block.s: Section 1886(r)(2)(B) of the Social Security Act, as added by section 3133, is amended— (1) in clause (i)— (A) in the matter preceding subclause (I), by striking “(divided by 100)”; (B) in subclause (I), by striking “2012” and inserting “2013”; (C) in subclause (II), by striking the period at the end and inserting a comma; and (D) by adding at the end the following flush matter:“minus 1.5 percentage points.”.

opus.w: This section only changes formula terms: it strikes "(divided by 100)", replaces 2012 with 2013, and subtracts 1.5 percentage points. It sets up no process for anyone outside the federal government to take part in a federal decision. It has no comment period, hearing, consultation, advisory body, rulemaking authority, or right to sue, so nothing in it is on-topic for participation.
opus.b: This section only makes technical amendments to Section 1886(r)(2)(B) of the Social Security Act, the Medicare payment formula. It changes years and subtracts percentage points. One could be tempted to read the formula change as a federal decision, but nothing in the text brings in outside parties: no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking authority, advisory body, or right to sue.
